chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from al-Walīd ibn ʿAlāʾ, from Ḥammād, from his father, from Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), who said:

Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, when He loves a servant, He immerses him thoroughly in affliction and pours affliction upon him abundantly. Then when he calls upon Him, He says: “Here I am, My servant. If I hasten for you what you asked, indeed I am able to do that; and if I store it up for you, then what I have stored up for you is better for you.”

key_terms.أَحَبَّ: loved; indicating divine favor toward the servant
key_terms.ادَّخَرْتُ: I stored up; meaning to reserve reward or response for later
key_terms.اللَّهَ: Allah, the Divine Being who lovingly tests and responds to His servant
key_terms.الْبَلَاءِ: affliction or trial through which the servant is tested
key_terms.خَيْرٌ: better; indicating the superior benefit in what Allah reserves
key_terms.دَعَاهُ: called upon Him; referring to making du'a
key_terms.عَجَّلْتُ: I hastened; meaning to give the requested matter immediately
key_terms.لَبَّيْكَ: Here I am; an expression of divine response to the servant’s call

ai.seo_question: Why does Allah afflict a believer whom He loves?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that affliction may be a sign of Allah’s love for a servant, not a sign of abandonment. It also shows that when a believer makes du'a, Allah may answer immediately or reserve something better for him, both being within divine wisdom and mercy.
